source.title: Establishment of Neural Networks Robust to Label Noise
source.authors: Pengwei Yang; Angel Teng; Jack Mangos

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling affects the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how class-dependent label noise affects LeNet and AlexNet test accuracy, using top-1 accuracy rather than the original studies' random-label fitting measures.
record.gate_note: The paper tests class-dependent label noise on FashionMINIST0.5, FashionMINIST0.6 and CIFAR. It does not report training error, random labeling, fitting time, unstructured inputs, regularizer removal, or learning order. Transition-matrix estimator results are not rows because they do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study motivates noise correction using networks' propensity to memorize noisy labels, but measures clean-test accuracy and correction performance rather than memorization. Its two class-dependent noise settings do not establish perfect training fit or smooth degradation across a corruption sweep.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they describe both architectures as robust on the FashionMINIST datasets and say inadequate tuning and resource constraints prevent establishing correction benefits. Their discussion of no positive correction effect on FashionMINIST0.6 and CIFAR is inconsistent with Table 2's higher corrected mean accuracies; the conclusion should remain attributed to the authors.
record.recipe_differences: Uses class-dependent label noise and backward transition-matrix correction with LeNet and AlexNet; does not use the original random-label fitting setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that backward correction required a smaller learning rate. They also report that results varied with transition-matrix estimates and model tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Without correction, LeNet test accuracy falls from 91.96% to 75.63%, and AlexNet from 90.23% to 82.28%, between the two FashionMINIST noise settings. Training fit is unreported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clean-test accuracy decreases between these two class-dependent label-noise settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 compares clean-test accuracy with and without backward correction on three datasets; these are robustness and mitigation outcomes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Backward correction changes clean-test classification performance under class-dependent label noise.

record.problems: The authors state that models were not finely tuned because of time and computing constraints; some models may not have converged to the optimum. The CIFAR transition matrix was estimated, and its accuracy was uncertain. Results report test accuracy, not training fit.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported outcome rows were omitted. Transition-matrix estimator comparisons are excluded because they do not measure a claim version.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels to zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative fitting time for real and random labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout a corruption sweep from none to all, steady test-error progression toward chance, and simultaneous signal learning and noise memorization.
Effects of adding or removing explicit regularization on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: The introduction cites the original random-label study for memorization; it does not reproduce that result. Figures 5–7 concern test accuracy, not training-label memorization. Smaller learning rates required for backward correction do not test V2's real-label versus random-label fitting-time comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training time and convergence speed as label corruption increases.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
The paper reports test accuracy at two noisy dataset settings, but not training error or perfect fitting; it does not test a sweep from no corruption to all labels corrupted.
No comparison tests whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation affect fitting random labels or true-label generalization.
No measurement of learning order or comparison of real and random labels over training.
